edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. in Cant. Prologus 4

source_text: Salomon interpretatur pacificus. Et vere pacificus hic liber est, in quo sponsus et sponsa in unum foedus pacis et caritatis conveniunt. Quomodo enim pax fieri potest nisi ubi caritas regnat? Et quomodo caritas nisi ubi Christus, qui est pax nostra, habitat? Ideo Salomon pacificus scribit Canticum Canticorum, ut pacificos ad pacem Christi introducat.
pass_a_gloss: Solomon is-interpreted peaceful. And truly peaceful this book is, in which bridegroom and bride into one covenant of-peace and charity come-together. How indeed peace to-happen can unless where charity reigns? And how charity unless where Christ who is peace our dwells?
pass_b_english: Solomon is interpreted peaceful. And truly this book is peaceful, in which Bridegroom and Bride come together into one covenant of peace and charity. For how can peace come about except where charity reigns? And how charity, except where Christ, who is our peace, dwells? Therefore Solomon the Peaceful writes the Song of Songs, that he may bring peaceful people into the peace of Christ.
